name: Cyber Grape
lede: Cyber Grape is a dark, dusky violet-purple from Crayola's crayon list, dark enough that the ISCC-NBS system reads it as a moderate violet rather than a true purple.

sections.title: A Crayola name, undocumented beyond that
sections.body: Our only record of this name traces to Wikipedia's inventory of Crayola crayon names; Crayola does not publish an explanation of the choice, and when the crayon entered the line is undocumented in the sources we have [1]. The ISCC-NBS system classifies the hex value as a moderate violet, about 2.5 units from that block's reference color, and the Munsell notation works out to 1.4P 3.2/7.6, low in lightness and middling in chroma [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[anthracene-violet]], [[imperial-purple]], [[hyacinth-blue]] and [[corsican-blue]], at 4.6, 4.6, 4.6 and 5 ΔE [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to this color in only 7 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.03 percent, and in 6 by the stricter within-painting measure, making it rarer than 73 percent of the named colors we track [3]. The earliest match dates to 1875, attributed to Alfred Sisley, with the latest from 1929, only 4 dated paintings in all, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. That is a thin record even by the standards of a modern, saturated color name invented for a crayon box rather than taken from paint or dye history [2][3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[3].

openers: Cyber Grape is a Crayola name with no documented explanation -- not even a date for when the crayon appeared.
Despite the name, Cyber Grape reads as a moderate violet in the ISCC-NBS system, not a true grape-red purple.
